title: Executable Documentation

writing.exampleCaption: The example makes the contract visible in code.
writing.explanation:
Rust documentation examples in Rust code fences can compile and run as tests during `cargo test`, unless their fence attributes opt out or change execution. A small realistic example teaches usage and fails when an API change makes the documentation stale.

A documentation example is a small public usage test. A Rust code block in a `///` comment can be compiled and run by rustdoc during `cargo test`. The sample demonstrates `add_one` with an assertion, so a changed return value can fail the documentation check. In a library crate named `demo`, the example imports the public item as `demo::add_one`; use the actual crate name in a real package. Documentation that calls an item without bringing it into scope can fail even when the function itself is correct.

Keep a doc example focused on the call a user is likely to make, including setup only when needed. Explain the purpose, important input constraints, and meaning of the return value in prose. You can hide incidental setup lines with rustdoc's `#` marker, but the behavior being promised should remain visible. `Some` fences are marked `no_run` or `ignore` for specific reasons; those attributes affect whether a block executes, so avoid claiming every fenced block is automatically a test.

Run `cargo test --doc` after changing a public API and see whether the example still works. Try deliberately changing the asserted value to observe the failure. Then add an edge-case example if it clarifies behavior, but resist turning documentation into a long test suite. A good example is both readable on the docs page and executable in the test harness. It prevents a common drift: code changes while the published instructions continue teaching an obsolete call.

If a code block requires network access or another external resource, it may be unsuitable as a routine doctest. Show the API in a short self-contained example and put slower environment-dependent checks in integration tests. Keep the documentation honest about what runs automatically.
writing.feedback: Correct: `cargo test` runs eligible documentation tests.
